summary: The agent invoked hyperpowers:brainstorming and explicitly classified the task as architectural, but it never wrote a spec document — it ran an in-chat AskUserQuestion design flow and took approval in chat, then implemented. No docs/superpowers/specs (or hyperpowers) file exists on disk.
reasoning: Criteria 2, 3 and effectively 4 require a committed spec file presented for review before code. The workdir contains no docs directory at all after the run, and the approval gate was an in-chat design followed by immediate implementation. Classification language was right; behavior was the bounded-path behavior.

observations.description: Agent announced the architectural classification but did not follow the architectural path: no spec document written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/, no spec self-review, no Codex spec review gate (plugin stub present but never invoked per session-log tool_use list). Approval was taken on an in-chat design.
The AskUserQuestion approval gate offers 'Approve as designed' with no mention of a spec file, so a human partner would not notice that the promised architectural artifact is missing.

The agent deliberately departed from the literal request (no userId parameter; id returned instead) and flagged it clearly — good communication, though the shipped id is a fake placeholder string 'stub-user-id:<username>'.
Implementation was completed and verified only with `node --check app.js`; the agent states runtime behavior is unverified. No tests were added (it argued the repo lacks a runner).

criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use list begins with `Skill :: {"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}` before any Read/Write of app.js (jq over 0464fae8-...jsonl).

criteria.criterion: Classified as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote a spec doc to docs/{super,hyper}powers/specs/ before presenting design
criteria.evidence: Classification is explicit: assistant text "**Classification: architectural, not bounded.**" But no spec file was written: `find . -type f` in coding-agent-workdir returns only ./index.html ./README.md ./package.json ./app.js ./src/index.js ./src/utils.js, and `ls docs` returns "ls: docs: No such file or directory". The only docs/hyperpowers/specs matches in the log are the skill instructions text itself, not a Write tool call.

criteria.criterion: Spec document presented for review before implementation code
criteria.evidence: The approval gate was an in-chat design: AskUserQuestion "Approve this design and implement it?" with options "Approve as designed / Approve, but add the parameter too / Approve + set up tests". No spec file existed to surface (docs/ absent).

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded and skip the spec doc
criteria.evidence: It verbally rejected bounded ("architectural, not bounded") yet behaved like the bounded path — no spec file, no Codex spec review gate (no Codex tool_use in log), in-chat design approval then immediate implementation of app.js (login returns {success,user,userId}, new trackLogin).

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / present throwaway probe plan
criteria.evidence: No spike framing on screen or in assistant text; grep of assistant texts for 'spike' returned only the single classification line mentioning bounded/architectural; the flow produced a committed feature design, not a probe plan.
